hints: When a warm day finally comes, it may settle the wait for several earlier, colder days at once. Which earlier days are still 'waiting'?
Keep a stack of day indices whose temperatures never increase from bottom to top. A warmer day pops the colder days and the wait is the index difference.

1. Fill ans with 0; create an empty stack.
  2. For each day i: while the stack is not empty and temps[top] < temps[i], pop j and set ans[j] = i - j.
  3. Push i.
  4. Days left on the stack keep 0. Return ans.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: For every day, scan forward until a warmer day appears.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Monotonic stack of waiting days; each day is pushed and popped at most once.

explain: Take temps = [61,58,63,63,70,52]. Days 0 and 1 are pushed. Day 2 (63) pops day 1 (wait 1) and day 0 (wait 2). Day 3 is also 63, which is not strictly warmer, so it is just pushed. Day 4 (70) pops day 3 (wait 1) and day 2 (wait 2). Day 5 (52) is pushed, and days 4 and 5 are never popped, so they stay 0. Result: [2,1,2,1,0,0]. Remember the strict <: an equal temperature is not warmer.
recognize: 'How many days until a bigger value' → monotonic stack of indices.
